subject: Re: Dedicated reservation sizing / proposed next steps (Acme Health RFI)
messages:
From: Ben Walters <ben.walters@acmehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Anita Rao <anita.rao@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity RFI - sizing inputs and target SLA

Hannah —

Thanks for taking this RFI. Acme Health is preparing an enterprise procurement packet for a dedicated inference reservation to support our clinical document processing workloads. We're evaluating dedicated pools with predictable throughput and a burst lane for peak windows. High level constraints:
- Target steady-state throughput: 18M tokens/day (avg) with 3x diurnal peak windows.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 200ms for single-turn completion on our 8k-sequence prompts.
- Model mix: two primary families — a 13B encoder-decoder for structured extraction and a 70B decoder for long-context summarization.
- Expected concurrency: 1,200 qps (avg peak), spiking to 3,500 qps for short windows.
- Data residency: US-only.

Can you provide: recommended GPU families & counts for a reserved baseline + recommended burst pool sizing, expected tokens/s per GPU for both model classes, KV-cache sizing guidance, and any recommended canary/rollout approach for the reservation?

Attached: ACME_RFP_dedicated_questions.pdf (list of RFP questions).

Timing: we aim to finalize vendor selections by the end of March. Would like an initial sizing worksheet and mutual action plan by next week if possible.

Ben
Procurement — Acme Health

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Ben Walters <ben.walters@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity RFI - sizing inputs and target SLA

Ben —

Thanks for the clear requirements and the attached PDF. Quick clarifying questions before we produce the workbook:
1) For the 70B summarization model, are you running full autoregressive decoding at generation-time or using a paraphrase/condense step (shorter outputs)? This affects per-token compute.
2) Your "8k-sequence prompts" — is that maximum context length (including history) or average?
3) Do you anticipate large embedding lookups or dense retrieval steps prior to generation?

We'll put together a conservative baseline + burstable plan and include two sizing scenarios (latency-optimized and cost-optimized). Karthik will own the initial GPU-throughput estimates and Laura will draft the reservation/contract sketch.

Would a 30-minute sizing workshop tomorrow 10:00 AM PT work for your engineering/ML ops team? We can walk the workbook live and lock on assumptions.

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Walters <ben.walters@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity RFI - sizing inputs and target SLA

Ben / Hannah —

Following Hannah's questions, Ben confirmed in the call that: the 70B runs standard autoregressive decode (avg output length ~1,200 tokens for summarization) and 8k is the maximum context (median ~2.5k). No heavy vector DB lookups — retrieval is batched pre-tokenization.

Preliminary sizing assumptions (conservative):
- Models: "Open-13B" (encoder-decoder) and "Open-70B" (decoder-only).
- Hardware candidates: NVIDIA H100 (HBM, high throughput) and NVIDIA L4 (cost-efficient T4 successor) for small/light calls.

Throughput estimates (inference tokens/sec per GPU, running our quantized runtimes with 8k context, 95th-latency tuned):
- Open-13B: H100 @ 1x batch -> ~5,500 toks/sec; L4 @ 1x batch -> ~1,400 toks/sec
- Open-70B: H100 @ 1x batch -> ~1,100 toks/sec; L4 -> not recommended for production 70B (memory/latency tradeoffs)

Reservation planning:
- Baseline (predictable, committed): 10 H100s. Rationale: meets steady-state throughput with headroom for tail and maintenance (est: 10 H100s -> ~11M tokens/day for mixed model usage).
- Cost-optimized baseline (alternate): 6 H100s + 12 L4s (L4s serve steady light-weight 13B calls; H100s handle 70B and burst).
- Burst pool (reserved but preemptible / burst lane): additional 8 H100s for site-wide peaks (3x diurnal windows). Burst pool should be autoscaled via policy tied to queue depth + SLO violation rate.

KV-cache guidance: allocate ~0.7GB per concurrent 8k session on H100 for decoder KV; plan for shared LRU prefix cache with 64GB total reserved RAM across the pool (adjust after 1-week traffic sample).

Canary & rollout:
- Canary window: 48 hours on 2 H100s serving 5% of traffic with regression monitoring (quality/eval prompts) + tail-latency SLO monitoring.
- Gradual ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over three days if no regressions or SLO breaches.

Attached is the sizing workbook (redwood_gpu_sizing_workbook.xlsx) with scenario tabs and calculation cells. We'll include tokenization assumptions and per-model compute curves.

-Karthik
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Walters <ben.walters@acmehealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 12:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Proposed reservation structure & commercial sketch

Ben / team —

Based on Karthik's sizing and your targets, here's a pragmatic reservation we recommend along with high-level commercial terms:

Recommended reservation (Preferred SLO profile):
- Committed baseline: 12 GPUs (8 x H100, 4 x L4) — supports steady state and provides cross-model headroom.
- Guaranteed burst pool: 10 H100s available as a "burst lane" for scheduled windows or autoscale triggers. Burst capacity is metered separately and billed at a burst rate.
- Canary: 2 H100s isolated in a private VPC subnet for rollout testing.

Operational controls & mitigations:
- Routing policy: route 70B traffic to H100s only; 13B traffic preferred to L4s where latency permits.
- Autoscaling guardrails: queue depth + 95th-latency > 150ms triggers burst lane.
- Maintenance window: 2x nodes maintenance at a time; failover routing to burst pool during maintenance.

Commercial sketch (draft):
- Term: 12 months with quarterly usage reviews and one contract renewal option.
- Pricing: blended committed rate for baseline + pay-as-you-go burst billing.
- SLA: 99.9% availability for baseline pool; remediation credit model outlined in attached contract draft.

Attachments included: acme_proposed_reservation_contract_v1.pdf (contract sketch), reservation_topology_diagram.png (topology & routing).

Next steps:
1) Quick workshop to confirm traffic shape and finalize the workbook assumptions (Hannah suggested 30 min).
2) Redwood sends a formal quotation (line-item pricing + DocuSign) after workshop.

If this looks reasonable we'll prepare a DocuSign package and schedule a follow-up with your procurement/legal teams.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
